source.title: AdapterGNN: Efficient Delta Tuning Improves Generalization Ability in Graph Neural Networks
source.authors: Sheng-Rui Li; Xueting Han; Jing Bai

page_placements.theme: Actual interpolation and evaluation design determine whether a peak appears

record.file_problem: Whole paper text, including appendices, is present. Some figure content is flattened, so exact plotted values cannot be recovered from the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly sweeps GNN model size and training-data size and reports outcomes that challenge the proposed double-descent and more-data-can-hurt patterns in its tested settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-size sweeps and training-data-size sweeps relevant to the claim. Results shown only in plots are recorded as figure only; exact curve values are not stated. The study does not report an epoch-wise sweep, a peak located at an interpolation threshold, or tests of label noise or regularization dependence.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps GNN size (from scratch) and training-data fraction (fine-tuning), but says training error never approaches zero, so its models stay below the interpolation threshold. Every version places the peak or the second descent at or beyond that threshold. The U-shaped curves therefore cannot confirm or refute any version; the authors use them only to justify a 'classical regime' premise for PEFT.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it should be stated explicitly that the authors place their tasks in the classical regime because training error never approaches zero. They do not claim to have looked for, or ruled out, double descent past interpolation. Their main conclusion is that AdapterGNN (PEFT) beats full fine-tuning with fewer parameters and smaller generalization gaps.
record.recipe_differences: Empirical GNN size and data-size sweeps, rather than a reproduction of the original double-descent experiments; includes both training-from-scratch and fine-tuning settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports size sweeps using two size definitions (embedding dimension and MLP middle dimension); the training-data experiments differ by dataset and tuning method.

fits_no_version.finding: GIN trained from scratch on six molecular datasets shows a single U-shaped test-error curve over embedding and MLP-middle dimension, with training error staying well above zero up to the largest sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the GNN molecular-property tasks tested, models up to embedding 1000 / MLP-middle 3000 do not interpolate, and test error follows the classical U-shape.

record.problems: The model-size and training-data results relevant here are presented as plots without exact values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The authors state that training error does not approach zero in the model-size experiments, so the interpolation threshold is not tested. The data-size sweeps do not identify a near-threshold region.

untested.parts: Whole version: sweeps never reach the size that fits the training set, so no peak or second descent can be assessed.
No sample sweep near the interpolation threshold.
Only GIN GNNs, and no interpolation point is reached.

missing.what: Model-size sweep under full fine-tuning of pre-trained GIN: average and BBBP ROC-AUC rise then fall with embedding dimension, and the Tox21 generalization gap grows with size. This is also sub-interpolation, so it bears on no version, but it is the paper's main-text size result.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' labels are unjustified. Double descent predicts nothing below the interpolation threshold, which the authors themselves say is never reached (they cite Nakkiran et al. for this criterion). Rows r14, r15, r17 and r18 compare the study's own method and should be unlinked. All values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: No peak location relative to the size that just fits the training set is identified; the reported sweeps are not shown to reach interpolation.
No test-error sweep over training epochs or time is reported.
The study does not identify or test a region near an interpolation threshold.
The empirical tests concern GNNs, not a broad range of model classes; they do not establish behavior beyond the tested GNN settings.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.
No tests of label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization are reported.
The study does not re-count complexity using an effective parameter measure to test whether a second descent becomes an ordinary U-shape.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study contrasts classical and over-parameterized generalization regimes and discusses prior double-descent work, while grounding its own PEFT analysis in the classical regime.

tranche.reason: Appendix C.1 reports classical U-shaped capacity sweeps with training error not approaching zero. Figure 5 reports data-size effects without establishing a near-interpolation region. Neither supplies a test of the listed double-descent versions.

source_check.notes: Rows r1–r12 are coverage-only observations; their version links should be ["none"], while cannot_determine is appropriate. Nonzero training error is explicitly reported for the from-scratch sweeps; it is not demonstrated for every fine-tuning condition.
